We focus on two recent LLM-based evaluation methods: GPTScore and an extended version of G-Eval, which we coin GPTRank. These methods are used to score or rank candidate summaries after generation.

We formulate the human evaluation as a summary pairwise comparison task. We use Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for the crowd‑annotation collection. The summary pairs are compared on three aspects: (1) salience, (2) coherence, and (3) overall preference/quality, where the annotators are required to choose which summary is better (ties are allowed).
We use Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for the crowd-annotation collection. Each data example is annotated by three annotators who are given two minutes for one task and compensated accordingly.
